_note: Each assignment's learning objectives, owned by the student: one "I can" sentence per competency, naming the skill and how this task's work shows it. Draft 1 (2026-10-24) was written to the student ("You ..."); draft 2 rewrites it in the student's voice (the operator's direction, 2026-10-24). Approved by the teacher 2026-10-24 (meta/STUDENT_WORK_PLAN_2026-10.md). Once approved, the reflection questions quote them (00's REFLECTION_FRAMES) and the doc shows them under What your work needs to show. Not read by any code yet. _concerns lists tertiary competencies whose task gives little room to show them; the teacher kept all of them (2026-10-24).

_concerns.why: The task traces the eras of marketing, not the history of the sports, entertainment, and event industries, so only an indirect link is possible.
The task is about personal support communities, not industry contacts, so no part of it asks for a networking plan in the industry.
The reflection never asks students to name or compare types of customer interaction, so the criterion goes beyond the questions asked.
No analysis point asks why the business or industry matters to customers or the community.
The research questions cover cost, revenue, stadiums and the economy but never supply and demand directly.
Nothing in the pizza task mentions competitors, so competition can only show up indirectly in the pricing justification.
No part of the scouting report asks about how the team or company is managed; the criterion stretches Part 2 (ownership) to the closest fit.
Part 2 asks for the ownership type and how you know, not its advantages or disadvantages, so this would only show if the student goes beyond the task.
The pitch is written only; nothing in the task has the student speak, present or listen.
The letter asks for the hook, connection, value and call to action, not what the sponsor money pays for, and tournament costs are not given.
The task asks for a brand board, not promotion, pricing or partnerships, so no part of it really asks for a marketing plan.
